name: Grey Foster
home: the streets inland from Pier Beach
life: “I used to leave a spare fold in every apprentice's coat.” Tuesday often includes a stop at Lighthouse Cove, where Grey takes a few minutes by the low rocks, where conversation sounds different as the tide turns.
voice: I shortened the sleeve too far on purpose for a child to grow into it. I can reverse my own work.
appearance: Grey has gray hair trimmed very close behind the ears, a deep crease beside the mouth when smiling, and a favorite piece of clothing, a moss-green cardigan. It usually goes with a small enamel bird on the lapel. When somebody else has the floor, Grey gives a little nod before asking a hard question.
personality: Grey feels a room through sound. A door slammed in high spirits can produce the same instant startle as an angry one, and it takes a little while to hear what actually follows.
agenda: To reverse the old allowance before replacing good cloth.
family: Cara Carvalho is Grey’s first cousin once removed. Grey asks before bringing somebody along. Cara can always ask for five minutes alone. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *The first language*, Cara says, “I can read every word but my classmates think my voice changes when I do.”
connections: Amira Lam. The donated button makes sense to the tailor who left cloth for growth.

reactions.response: Grey asks the applicant whether a whole donated suit would actually be welcome.

reactions.situation: A cyclist goes down in a crowded crossing
reactions.response: Grey moves the onlookers' bags out of the way, asks the rider what hurts, and asks one named bystander to call for help.

reactions.situation: If an argument gets loud at home
reactions.response: Grey lowers their own voice and asks for one thought at a time.
